source: Q148 (2026-09-23): owner complaint that the specimen viewers upper body "structures have moved" -- fixes the intervertebral disc placement generator (scripts/generate_intervertebral_discs.py) on both ct_vhm/ct_vhf, and a systematic misplacement audit of both rebuilt viewer bundles. No external literature; internal geometry-consistency audit only. See PROJECT_STATE.md's Q148 entry.

part1_intervertebral_discs.bug: Every disc in a region shared one fixed X/Y (region-wide bbox center) and was spread only along Z (this atlas's ANTERIOR axis) by fraction of level index -- front-to-back instead of stacked between vertebrae along Y (craniocaudal). Lumbar had the same symptom on the male subject because its OBJ files were never regenerated after Q111's lumbar-only per-level fix (mtime + value match to the pre-Q111 numbers confirmed this, not assumed).
root_cause: create_cylinder_mesh built the disc's thickness axis on Z and radius on XY, when +Y is this atlas's craniocaudal axis (frame: +X right, +Y superior, +Z anterior) -- every disc's 40mm radius therefore landed in Y, ~80mm tall regardless of the true ~10-40mm inter-vertebral gap.
cervical/thoracic centers were a single region-wide bbox X/Y (Q111 fixed lumbar only, generalized here to all three regions).
part1_intervertebral_discs.fix: scripts/generate_intervertebral_discs.py: create_cylinder_mesh's axis swapped to Y (radius now XZ); compute_lumbar_disc_centers generalized to compute_region_vertebra_pieces + compute_level_disc_centers, used for cervical/thoracic/lumbar alike. Vertebra fragments identified by sorting each region's manifest records by mean Y descending (7 cervical/12 thoracic/5 lumbar records per subject, one per real vertebra, count-verified) -- no per-vertebra name/label id needed, so it works on ct_vhm (which lacks one) same as ct_vhf.
verification: Regenerated all 21x2 disc OBJs and re-ran ingest_intervertebral_discs.py into build/vh/ct_vhm and build/vh/ct_vhf.
Centroids strictly increase in Y from L4-L5 up to C1-C2 on both subjects (tests/test_intervertebral_discs.py::test_disc_centroids_strictly_increase_in_y_bottom_to_top).
Each disc's Y lies between its two adjacent vertebrae's own mean Y (tests/test_intervertebral_discs.py::test_each_disc_lies_between_its_two_adjacent_vertebrae).
Before/after sagittal renders (scratchpad disc_fix_male.png / disc_fix_female.png): discs collapsed into 3 front-to-back blobs before, tracking the spine's real curve after.

disc_volume.note: identical across all 21 levels x 2 subjects: same procedural 40mm-radius/20mm-thick cylinder at every level, not an anatomical measurement

part2_misplacement_audit.method: Decoded build/viewer_m/atlas_viewer_male.html and build/viewer_f/atlas_viewer_female.html (bundle-json + bundle-b64) after the Q148 disc rebuild. (a) sided-midline: for every atlas_id ending _l/_r, centroid x vs. a piecewise spine x(y) built from every vertebra fragment's own centroid; _r must have x > spine x at its level. (b) muscle centroid vs. the bbox union of its origin_bone/insertion_bone (from data/muscles/**/*.json attachments), flagged if >40mm outside; also flagged any structure bbox entirely outside the subject's own skin bbox (+20mm pad). (c) per-subject-block (the 'subject' field the bundle carries per structure) _l/_r pair midpoint vs. spine x at that level, flagged if >15mm off.

assessment.sided_midline: Essentially clean. Female geniohyoid_r at delta -1.2mm (barely past the spine line, near-midline structure) -- measurement noise, not a real left/right swap. No action.
assessment.far_from_attachment: 13 muscles flagged (gastrocnemius, sternocleidomastoid, biceps/triceps brachii, forearm extensors, styloglossus, lateral_rectus, coccygeus, etc.), all across both subjects. Manual review: every one is a normal two-joint or long muscle whose belly legitimately occupies the natural gap between its two named attachment bones' bboxes (e.g. gastrocnemius's femur bbox and tarsal bbox do not overlap -- the whole calf is a 'gap' by this bbox-union metric that the muscle correctly fills). NOT filed as placement bugs; noted as a limitation of the >40mm-outside-bbox heuristic for any muscle whose attachments span an intervening unlisted bone (tibia/fibula, radius/ulna, humerus shaft).
assessment.block_symmetry: 3 male pairs just past the 15mm threshold: gastrocnemius 16.5mm, soleus 15.1mm (both vhm_both block), phalanges_hand 16.0mm (ct_vhm_arm block). Plausible natural limb-pose asymmetry in the source photography (nothing like the abw's ~100mm mirror offset) -- queued for a visual check rather than fixed blind.
